Date: Sun, 10 Jan 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Priority throttling addendum — TradeData procurement

Hi Lauren,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We saw encouraging latency numbers against the Redwood hosted API but our legal/procurement team is asking for a narrow SLA addendum tied to peak market windows. Specifically:

- Objective: guarantee access to a short daily burst above our baseline quota during US market open (13:30–15:30 UTC).
- Burst allowance: 3x baseline token rate for a 2-hour window, once per trading day.
- Latency target: 95th percentile token latency <= 250ms within the priority window.
- Fairness policy carveout: requests from TradeData tagged with priority_token should not be subject to cross-customer fairshare throttles during the window; sustained abuse detection OK.
- Duration: initial term: 12 months with a review at month 6.

Attached is our peak traffic export so you can see the pattern (TD_peak_traffic_report.csv). Can Redwood provide language for an SLA appendix and a rough price uplift for a reserved priority token pool?

We need this for procurement review the week of Jan 18–22. If possible, send a proposed addendum and term sheet by Jan 20.

Best,
Sam
Sam Park
Head of Platform Partnerships
TradeData AI

Lauren,

We can support a short priority window with some caveats. Technical summary below:

- Implementation: create a dedicated priority_token_pool per-customer that maps to an isolated token quota on the routing plane. During window, requests with X-Priority-Token header are routed to priority pool nodes.
- Fairness bypass: set routing weight to 100% for priority pool nodes for the 2-hour window; other customers still served on standard pool.
- Limits and safety: enforce a hard daily cap (e.g., 3x baseline * daily cap) and per-minute rate ceilings to prevent sustained overload.
- Latency guarantee: 95p <= 250ms is achievable on A100-ish hardware when KV caches are warm and under light cross-tenant load; warmup may take ~3–5 minutes after cold start. Recommend warm-up pre-roll (30 minutes) or slot reservation to ensure cache priming.
- Operational notes: require SRE-runbook updates, a canary period (30 days) and a rollback policy if latencies degrade.

Attached is a sample config snippet for the routing/pool (priority_pool_config.yaml). Pricing and contract language needed to proceed.

-Karthik

--

Lauren / team,

Pricing proposal (high-level):
- Reserved priority token pool for TradeData: 12-month commitment.
- Estimated uplift: +25% MRC relative to their existing reserved capacity. This covers reserved nodes, pre-warmed caches, and 24/7 SRE support for the priority window.
- Addendum term: 12 months, 30-day canary with termination/change clause.

Commercial caveats: any reduction of the priority window or sustained abusive traffic will trigger a review and possible rate-limiting back to baseline. Also we should include a credit schedule tied to missed SLOs (pro-rated token credits rather than cash).

Attached: pricing_term_sheet.xlsx (stub). I recommend we include explicit credit calculation examples in the addendum.

-Rishi

Subject: Priority throttling addendum — proposed language and next steps

Hi Sam / Priya,

Thanks for the clear ask and for sharing the traffic file. We've discussed feasibility internally and can offer the following proposed addendum language (excerpt):

--- excerpt start ---
1. Priority Token Pool: Redwood will create a customer-dedicated priority_token_pool for TradeData AI. Requests with the X-Priority-Token header will be routed to the priority pool during the Priority Window (13:30–15:30 UTC daily).
2. Burst Allowance: TradeData may consume up to 3x baseline token rate during the Priority Window, subject to a hard daily cap as specified in Schedule A.
3. Latency SLO: Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to maintain 95th percentile per-token latency <= 250ms within the Priority Window, provided that the priority pool has been provisioned and cache warm-up procedures have been followed. Credits for missed SLOs will be issued as token credits per Schedule B.
4. Fairness Carveout: During the Priority Window, traffic tagged with X-Priority-Token will not be subject to cross-customer fairshare throttling except in cases of detected abuse or system-wide emergency.
5. Canary and Rollback: A 30-day canary period will be executed on initial activation. Redwood reserves the right to throttle to baseline if sustained overload or abuse is detected.
--- excerpt end ---

Commercial proposal: 12-month reserved priority pool at +25% MRC with token-credit based SLA remedies.

Next steps: please review and redline the attached addendum (SLA_Addendum_Draft.docx). If agreeable, we can send via DocuSign for signatures — link below. Target for procurement review completion: Jan 22.

DocuSign (draft): https://www.docusign.net/Member/PowerFormSigning.aspx?PowerFormId=abc-td-2027
HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/record/TD-9876

Let me know if you need the latency target relaxed or any additional safeguards.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Priority throttling addendum — proposed language and next steps

Lauren — thanks for the quick turnaround and the clear draft. Procurement reviewed and asked for one modest change before we can sign: relax the latency SLO to 95th percentile <= 300ms (from 250ms). They want this to account for occasional cross-region variability and to avoid expensive overprovisioning. Everything else looks fine; pricing uplift is acceptable.

If you can update the excerpt and resend the DocuSign link, we can execute by Jan 22.

Cheers,
Sam
